questions.question_text: In a pictograph where 1 bicycle symbol = 6 bicycles, how many symbols represent 42 bicycles?
Tally marks are grouped in bundles of:
Convert the tally mark expression '||||/  ||||/  |||' into a frequency integer.
Monthly family food expenditure is Rs 3600. On a scale of 1 cm = Rs 400, find the bar height.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Bar Height = 3600 / 400 = 9 cm.

questions.question_text: A cricketer took the following wickets in 10 matches: 2, 3, 0, 4, 2, 5, 1, 3, 2, 4. Prepare a frequency table for wickets taken.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 0 wkts: 1; 1 wkt: 1; 2 wkts: 3; 3 wkts: 2; 4 wkts: 2; 5 wkts: 1. Total matches = 10.

questions.question_text: State the three essential rules for drawing a mathematically accurate bar graph.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Uniform bar width. 2. Equal gaps between adjacent bars. 3. Vertical scale starting at baseline 0.

questions.question_text:
Case Study: Traffic Survey Data. Vehicle counts passing a junction in 1 hour: Cars = 25, Bikes = 40, Buses = 10, Autos = 15.
(a) What is the total vehicle count? (2 marks)
(b) What fraction of total traffic is two-wheelers (Bikes)? (3 marks)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(a) Total = 25 + 40 + 10 + 15 = 90 vehicles.
(b) Bike fraction = 40 / 90 = 4/9.

questions.question_text: Raw data means:
If 1 tree icon = 10 trees, 4.5 icons represent:
Represent frequency 18 using standard tally marks.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: ||||/  ||||/  ||||/  ||| (3 full bundles of 5 plus 3 vertical strokes).

questions.question_text: In a bar graph, category A has frequency 50 and category B has frequency 200. Compare their bar heights.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Category B bar height is 200/50 = 4 times taller than Category A bar height.

questions.question_text: Given test scores of 15 students: 5, 8, 6, 7, 5, 8, 9, 6, 5, 7, 8, 5, 6, 7, 8. Find the mode (score with highest frequency).
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Score 5: 4 times; Score 6: 3 times; Score 7: 3 times; Score 8: 4 times; Score 9: 1 time. Modes are 5 and 8 (bimodal, frequency 4).

questions.question_text: Explain how truncating the vertical axis (not starting at 0) creates visual distortion in a bar graph.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Starting the scale above 0 exaggerates visible height differences between bars, making small relative differences appear artificially huge.

questions.question_text:
Case Study: School Library Book Survey. Book counts by genre: Fiction = 250, Science = 150, History = 100, Sports = 50.
(a) Calculate bar heights for a scale of 1 cm = 50 books. (2 marks)
(b) Find the ratio of Fiction books to History books. (3 marks)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(a) Fiction = 250/50 = 5 cm; Science = 150/50 = 3 cm; History = 100/50 = 2 cm; Sports = 50/50 = 1 cm.
(b) Ratio = 250 : 100 = 5 : 2.

questions.question_text: In a pictograph, half a symbol represents:
Horizontal axis in a standard vertical bar graph represents:
Shoe sizes recorded: 4, 5, 4, 6, 5, 5, 4, 6, 5. Find the frequency of size 5.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Size 5 occurs 4 times. Frequency = 4.

questions.question_text: Convert frequency 22 into tally marks.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: ||||/  ||||/  ||||/  ||||/  || (4 bundles of 5 plus 2 strokes).

questions.question_text: A pictograph shows 5 apple icons for Monday and 8 apple icons for Tuesday. If 1 icon = 12 kg, find total apples sold over both days.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Total icons = 5 + 8 = 13 icons. Total sales = 13 x 12 = 156 kg.

questions.question_text: Represent monthly savings on a bar graph scale of 1 cm = Rs 500: Jan = Rs 2000, Feb = Rs 3500, Mar = Rs 1500.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Jan height = 2000/500 = 4 cm; Feb height = 3500/500 = 7 cm; Mar height = 1500/500 = 3 cm.

questions.question_text:
Case Study: Garden Flower Count. Flower species count in a botanical garden: Rose = 120, Lily = 80, Sunflower = 60, Jasmine = 40.
(a) What percentage of total flowers are Roses? (2 marks)
(b) Construct a pictograph representation scheme choosing an appropriate key scale. (3 marks)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(a) Total flowers = 120 + 80 + 60 + 40 = 300. Rose percentage = (120 / 300) x 100 = 40%.
(b) Choose Key: 1 flower icon = 20 flowers. Icon counts: Rose = 6 icons, Lily = 4 icons, Sunflower = 3 icons, Jasmine = 2 icons.

questions.question_text: Which data presentation tool uses picture symbols with a declared scale key?
Frequency of a data value means:
options: B. Number of times it occurs
questions.correct_answer: B. Number of times it occurs

questions.question_text: If 1 cm = 8 units on Y-axis, calculate bar height for frequency 56.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Height = 56 / 8 = 7 cm.

questions.question_text: Given data: 12, 15, 12, 18, 15, 12, 20. Find the difference between the maximum frequency value and minimum frequency value.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Frequencies: 12 (3 times), 15 (2 times), 18 (1 time), 20 (1 time). Max frequency value = 12 (freq 3), Min frequency value = 18 or 20 (freq 1). Difference in frequencies = 3 - 1 = 2.

questions.question_text: Draw tally mark distribution for test marks out of 5: 3, 4, 2, 5, 3, 4, 3, 5, 4, 3, 2, 4, 3.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Mark 2: || (freq 2); Mark 3: ||||/ (freq 5); Mark 4: |||| (freq 4); Mark 5: || (freq 2). Total = 13.

questions.question_text: Explain why bar widths must be identical across all categories in a bar graph.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Varying bar widths misleads the viewer because visual area depends on both width and height. Equal widths ensure visual area is strictly proportional to height and frequency.

questions.question_text:
Case Study: Student Transport Survey. Mode of transport count for 120 students: Bus = 50, Walking = 30, Bicycle = 25, Car = 15.
(a) Find the ratio of students using Bus to those using Bicycle. (2 marks)
(b) Find the central angle percentage share for Walking students. (3 marks)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(a) Ratio Bus : Bicycle = 50 : 25 = 2 : 1.
(b) Percentage share = (30 / 120) x 100 = 25%. Corresponding central sector angle = 25% of 360° = 90°.

questions.question_text: In a bar graph, equal gaps must separate adjacent bars to maintain:
options: B. Uniform visual clarity and categorical distinction
questions.correct_answer: B. Uniform visual clarity and categorical distinction

questions.question_text: If 1 symbol = 25 students, 3 full symbols and 1 half symbol represent:
Convert frequency 27 into tally marks.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: ||||/  ||||/  ||||/  ||||/  ||||/  || (5 full bundles of 5 plus 2 vertical strokes).

questions.question_text: A bar graph Y-axis scale is 1 cm = 100 units. If bar height for Company X is 6.5 cm, find its revenue.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Revenue = 6.5 x 100 = 650 units.

questions.question_text: Given family monthly expenses: Rent = Rs 4000, Food = Rs 6000, Education = Rs 3000, Savings = Rs 2000. Calculate bar heights if scale is 1 cm = Rs 1000.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Rent = 4 cm; Food = 6 cm; Education = 3 cm; Savings = 2 cm.

questions.question_text: Compare pictographs and bar graphs in terms of precision and ease of drawing.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Pictographs use visual symbols (great for quick intuitive reading but hard to draw partial symbols accurately). Bar graphs use precise rectangular columns against a numerical axis (easier to construct and read exact values).
